title: Given k sorted lists, merge them into one sorted list efficiently using a priority queue (heap).
shortTitle: Merge K Sorted Lists Using a Min-Heap
keyPoints: Keep one candidate per list in a min-heap; poll the smallest, output it, and push that list's next element.
The heap holds at most k elements, so each poll and offer is O(log k), giving O(N log k) total time.
To know which list an element came from, wrap each value with its source index and position.
The naive concatenate-and-sort approach is O(N log N) and ignores the sorted order of each list.
This pattern is the core of external multi-way merge sort used for large sorted files.
The divide-and-conquer pairwise merge is an equally efficient O(N log k) alternative.
For money values, use BigDecimal with compareTo in the heap's comparator.

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep one candidate per list in a min-heap; poll the smallest, output it, and push that list's next element, for N log k total.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Min-heap of k fronts** – holds one element per list, ordered by value.
- **Poll and push** – extract the smallest, append to output, push the next element from that list.
- **O(N log k)** – each element is pushed and polled once at O(log k).
- **Source tracking** – wrap each value with its list index and position to know where to advance.
- **External merge** – this is exactly how multi-way merge sort combines sorted runs from disk.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine the National Bank of India has k branch ledgers, each already sorted by transaction time, and wants one combined ledger in time order. A clerk looks at the earliest unprocessed entry from each branch, picks the single earliest among them, writes it into the combined ledger, then looks at the next entry from just that branch. She keeps a tiny sorted tray with one entry per branch.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Merging k sorted lists means producing one sorted output by repeatedly taking the smallest unconsumed element across all lists. A min-heap holding one candidate from each list makes finding the smallest a O(log k) operation. You poll the smallest, append it, and push the next element from whichever list that one came from.

Because the heap only holds one representative per list, its size stays at most k, so every poll and push is O(log k). Over all N elements the total is O(N log k) with O(k) space. To track which list to advance, each heap entry stores its value, list index, and element position.

This is exactly how external merge sort combines sorted runs from disk. At the National Bank of India, end-of-day transaction files from several branches, each already sorted, are merged into one globally sorted file for settlement using this k-way merge.

The pairwise divide-and-conquer merge is an equally efficient alternative at O(N log k) without a heap. The heap version is simpler and naturally streaming.

Remember one sentence: keep one element per list in a min-heap, poll the smallest and push its successor, and the output comes out sorted in O(N log k) time.
